primary_diagnosis_treated: Diabetic nephropathy leading to end-stage renal disease (CKD stage 4)
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management) and NICE NG107 (Renal replacement therapy and conservative management)

medications.dose: 1.25 mg orally once daily (start low; titrate every 2‑4 weeks to target BP <130/80 mmHg)
medications.duration: Lifelong – review annually and titrate as needed
medications.purpose: Renoprotective and antihypertensive therapy for proteinuric CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE‑I for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension; monitor creatinine and potassium after dose changes

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CV‑risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 states all CKD patients should receive a statin for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 1000 mg IV single infusion (or 500 mg weekly until ferritin >200 µg/L or TSAT >20 %)
medications.duration: Single infusion; repeat only if iron studies remain deficient
medications.purpose: Correct iron deficiency before initiating ESA therapy for CKD‑related anaemia
medications.nice_justification: NG107 recommends IV iron for CKD anaemia when ferritin <200 µg/L or TSAT <20 %

medications.dose: 0.45 µg/kg subcutaneously every 2 weeks (adjust to maintain Hb 100‑120 g/L)
medications.duration: Until haemoglobin 100‑120 g/L achieved; then review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Treat anaemia of CKD when Hb <100 g/L after iron optimisation
medications.nice_justification: NG107 advises ESA for CKD anaemia (Hb <100 g/L) after iron repletion

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention; eGFR 4.2 mL/min/1.73 m²
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol or other non‑nephrotoxic analgesics as needed

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – risk of lactic acidosis
contraindications.alternative: Insulin or other glucose‑lowering agents with renal dosing guidance

contraindications.reason: Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury; patient already receiving ACE‑I
contraindications.alternative: If ACE‑I intolerant, switch to an ARB (e.g., losartan) rather than combine

contraindications.reason: High risk of hyperkalaemia in advanced CKD
contraindications.alternative: Dietary potassium restriction; monitor serum K⁺

contraindications.reason: Nephrotoxic and contraindicated in CKD stage 4
contraindications.alternative: Alternative mood stabilisers (e.g., valproate) after psychiatric review

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy
contraindications.alternative: Use non‑contrast imaging or low‑osmolar contrast with prophylactic hydration

contraindications.drug: Nephrotoxic antibiotics (e.g., gentamicin) without dose adjustment
contraindications.reason: Risk of accumulation and toxicity in severe CKD
contraindications.alternative: Choose renally‑adjusted antibiotics (e.g., ceftriaxone) and dose according to eGFR

assumptions_warnings: Baseline serum potassium not provided – required before starting ACE‑I and for ongoing monitoring (NG203).
Liver function tests not provided – required before initiating atorvastatin (NG203).
Full lipid profile (LDL‑C) not provided – statin intensity chosen based on CKD risk equivalence.
Hb, ferritin, TSAT, and iron studies not provided – iron infusion and ESA are conditional on documented deficiency/anemia.
Blood pressure reading not provided – titration of ramipril will be guided by actual BP values.
Allergy status unknown – must confirm no ACE‑I, statin, or iron preparation allergies before prescribing.
Phosphate, calcium, PTH, and bicarbonate levels not provided – phosphate binder and sodium bicarbonate are not prescribed until abnormalities are confirmed.
treatment_summary: The patient with CKD stage 4 secondary to diabetic nephropathy requires renoprotective ACE‑I therapy, high‑intensity statin for cardiovascular risk reduction, correction of iron deficiency, and ESA therapy for anaemia once iron stores are repleted. NSAIDs, metformin, dual RAAS blockade, and other nephrotoxic agents are contraindicated. Ongoing monitoring of renal function, electrolytes, lipids, haemoglobin, and iron status is outlined per NICE NG203 and NG107. Non‑pharmacological measures (BP target, low‑salt diet, smoking cessation, exercise) should be reinforced.
